name: FAUCET
what_it_is: FAUCET is an OpenFlow 1.3 SDN controller built on the Ryu framework that implements multi-table L2 switching, VLANs, ACLs, and L3 IPv4/IPv6 routing for both hardware and software switches. It is designed for production networks and exposes Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards for operational visibility.
components: faucet — main OpenFlow controller process, handles switch pipeline programming and policy enforcement
gauge — companion controller for monitoring; collects per-port and per-flow statistics independently of faucet
prometheus — time-series metrics store; scrapes faucet (port 9302) and gauge (port 9303) exporters
grafana — dashboarding service visualising Prometheus data; preconfigured dashboards ship with the repo
protocols: BGP (via ExaBGP integration for IPv4/IPv6 route exchange)
IPv4 and IPv6 (static and BGP-learned routes)
DHCP (relay, via external DHCP server integration)
measurement: Per-port byte/packet/error counters exported via Prometheus on port 9302 (faucet) and 9303 (gauge)
Per-flow match/action statistics collected by gauge and stored in time-series (Prometheus or InfluxDB)
Controller health and event loop latency exposed as Prometheus gauges
Grafana dashboards included for switch, port, and flow-level visualisation
Event socket (FAUCET_EVENT_SOCK) streams structured JSON events for external consumers
configuration: Single YAML file (faucet.yaml) declares all DPs, VLANs, ACLs, routers, and interfaces
gauge.yaml separately configures polling intervals, watchers, and storage backends
Hot-reload supported: FAUCET_CONFIG_STAT_RELOAD causes faucet to reload on config file change without restarting
Prometheus scrape targets and alert rules in etc/prometheus/; mounted as volume in compose
FAUCET_PREFIX env var controls host-side paths for logs, configs, and persistent storage volumes
fault_injection: No native fault-injection API; test harness (tests/) uses Mininet and OVS to simulate link failures and topology changes
Integration tests exercise failover scenarios across stacked datapaths and LAG groups
modes: Standalone controller — single faucet process managing one or more OpenFlow datapaths
Stacked/distributed — multiple datapaths connected in a stack topology with automated failover
Hardware switch mode — faucet programs physical OpenFlow-capable ASICs; OFA must pass pipeline integration tests
Software switch mode — runs against Open vSwitch (OVS) for development and CI
constraints: Requires OpenFlow 1.3 with multi-table support; switches that only support OpenFlow 1.0 are not supported
Hardware OFA must implement all matches defined in faucet's pipeline spec and pass integration tests — not all vendor ASICs qualify
BGP support depends on ExaBGP being deployed as a separate process; faucet does not embed a BGP daemon
802.1x and DHCP services require external processes (hostapd, dhcpd); faucet only handles the OpenFlow signalling side
gauge and faucet must share the same /etc/faucet volume to read a consistent topology; mismatched configs cause silent monitoring gaps
notable_absences: No built-in packet capture or PCAP export — requires external tap or OVS mirror port
No GUI for topology or policy editing — configuration is purely file-based YAML
No native chaos/fault-injection API — fault scenarios require external tooling (Mininet, manual OVS commands)
No embedded BGP daemon — ExaBGP must be deployed and integrated separately
docker-compose does not include an OVS/Mininet service — a software dataplane must be provisioned separately to have an end-to-end testable environment
